 Saints Could Part With Veterans at Bargain Price Before Deadline
 Originally posted on
 Athlon Sports 
  | 
 By Neal Coolong
  | 
 Last updated Nov 7, 2026 11:06 AM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 The New Orleans Saints came out of their bye at 2-5, and Kellen Moore promised to evaluate everything during the week off. The Saints have a roster full of veterans other teams have asked about, and the asking price might not be what fans expect.
 According to The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones , the Saints could deal a veteran or two at a low price if someone calls. That lines up with ESPN’s Katherine Terrell, who summed up the Saints’ deadline goal in four words: “Get what they can.”
 Which Saints veterans could be moved
 Oct 25, 2026; Paris, FRA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) is tackled by. New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid (21) during the second quarter at Stade de France Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
 Safety Justin Reid is the likeliest piece. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler named him New Orleans’ top trade candidate, noting that multiple teams need safety help , from Buffalo to Jacksonville. Reid is 29, has 124 career starts and started for two Super Bowl winners in Kansas City.
 His 2026 tape explains the bargain part. Measured against another safety on the market, Titans safety Amani Hooker, the gap is wide. Reid has a 44.4 PFF grade, 93rd of 98 qualified safeties, with no interceptions and a 131.9 passer rating allowed in coverage. Hooker has five interceptions and carried a 75.3 grade into Week 8. Teams won’t pay much for Reid’s version of this season.
 The Saints also won’t clear much money. New Orleans restructured several big contracts, and it sits at roughly $7.1 million in cap space , so most deals would speed up dead money rather than free room. That’s why a guard like Cesar Ruiz, with $22.5 million in dead money attached, is hard to move, and why an Alvin Kamara trade looks unlikely.
 For a rebuilding team, any pick is a win. Mickey Loomis can take a Day 3 selection for Reid and move on, and New Orleans will get one more look at its veterans when the Browns visit the Superdome on Sunday.
